problem.text: Find the number of eight-digit positive integers that are multiples of $9$ and have all distinct digits.

steps.title: Where to start: think about which two digits are missing
steps.body: A number is a multiple of $9$ exactly when its digit sum is a multiple of $9$. Eight distinct digits means we use all ten digits $0$ to $9$ except two. So instead of choosing eight digits, choose the two digits we leave out.

your_turn.prompt: What is $0 + 1 + 2 + \dots + 9$? What must be true about the two digits we leave out?
your_turn.answer: The sum is $45$, a multiple of $9$. The eight digits we keep sum to $45$ minus the two left out, so the two left-out digits must add to a multiple of $9$.

steps.title: List the possible missing pairs
steps.body: Two different digits add to at least $0 + 1 = 1$ and at most $8 + 9 = 17$, so their sum must be exactly $9$. That gives five pairs: $\{0,9\}$, $\{1,8\}$, $\{2,7\}$, $\{3,6\}$ and $\{4,5\}$.

your_turn.prompt: Why can the two left-out digits not add to $18$?
your_turn.answer: The only way to make $18$ with digits is $9 + 9$, but the two digits must be different.

steps.title: The pair $\{0,9\}$: no zero to worry about
steps.body: If we leave out $0$ and $9$, the digits $1$ to $8$ can be arranged in any order, since none of them is a leading zero. That gives $8!$ numbers.

steps.title: The other four pairs: keep $0$ out of the front
steps.body: For each of the other four pairs, the eight digits we keep include $0$, and an eight-digit number cannot start with $0$. Careful: $8!$ would overcount here. Place the $0$ first: it can go in any of the $7$ places except the first, and then the other $7$ digits fill the rest in $7!$ ways. So each pair gives $7 \cdot 7!$ numbers.

your_turn.prompt: Check this another way: of the $8!$ orderings of the eight digits, how many start with $0$?
your_turn.answer: $7!$ of them (fix $0$ in front, arrange the other seven). So $8! - 7! = 8 \cdot 7! - 7! = 7 \cdot 7!$ are valid, matching.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Add the one pair without $0$ and the four pairs with $0$:
$$8! + 4 \cdot 7 \cdot 7! = 8 \cdot 7! + 28 \cdot 7! = 36 \cdot 5040 = 181440.$$
The answer is **$181440$**.
